study type: Quality Improvement Study (Quasi-experimental cohort study with historical control)
exposure: Direct dispensing of prenatal supplements with iron during prenatal visits
Recommendation to obtain and take iron supplements
outcome: Maternal hematocrit levels (28-32 weeks, delivery admission, and discharge)
Postpartum transfusion for acute blood loss anemia
cohort: A total of 13,910 pregnant individuals, predominantly Hispanic, Medicaid-funded or self-pay, with a mean age of ~27-28 years, who delivered at Parkland Health, a safety net hospital in Dallas, Texas.
finding: Directly dispensing prenatal supplements with iron was associated with improved maternal hematocrit levels, reduced rates of anemia on admission, and a one-third reduction in postpartum transfusion for acute blood loss anemia.
followup_time: Up to hospital discharge after delivery
